meta.title: AI proof businesses worth building in 2027
meta.thread_line: 4 threads · paid peer groups · whale-funded communities · gacha/buyback card apps · Binance hack and DeFi

snapshot: Sam's pitch: you don't need to be an AI person — **communities** are businesses that grow with AI without being AI.
NADA 20 Groups: dealers pay ~$6-8k a year to sit with ~20 non-competing peers and go line by line through each other's P&L; Sam guesses $13-15M a year in revenue.
Moda Communities: a Sioux Falls founder runs ~20-25 Facebook groups (watches, cars, gold) with 600,000 members, funded by vetted dealers paying $1-10k a year.
Shaan's thread: **whales** fund everything — Candy Crush gets all its revenue from 4% of 82M monthly players; Twitch gifted subs worked because whales just needed new ways to spend.
Card-pack 'ripping' apps add a buyback ($43 back on a $50 pack) and one reportedly did ~$1B in a year; Collector Crypt runs ~$100M a month on-chain.
Mystery-box packaging lifted a toy maker's revenue 7x versus pick-what-you-want shelves.
Crypto aside: Binance hacked for $5B, with a ~$2B SAFU fund to cover it; Shaan calls DeFi completely overlooked and due to come back like prediction markets did.

themes.title: Boring-profession peer groups are durable cash machines
themes.lead: A paid, non-competing peer group for a high-income, unglamorous profession can run for decades, and AI doesn't touch it.
bullets: **NADA 20 Groups** (auto dealers, since roughly the 70s): apply, pay ~$6-8k a year, get placed in a group of ~20 dealers from other regions, meet three times a year, share P&Ls line by line.
Sam's estimate from published dues: $13-15M a year in revenue; the website and marketing are 'horrible', which is the opening. It later let in HVAC, marina and boat-repair owners.
His play: copy it a bit better and **run ads**, aimed at dentists, lawyers and other 'millionaire next door' professions rather than crowded e-com (his earlier Club LTV).
**White Coat Investor**: started as a blog, now media plus Facebook groups where doctors talk about their own money (rental cap rates, not medicine); Shaan sees room for a 2.0 on new media.

**BNI**: local chapters of non-competing businesses (realtor, garage doors, lawyer) trading leads, often meeting at the YMCA; ~800,000 members paying low thousands a year, recently acquired at a rumored $1B+.
The design rule: members are either non-competing by trade or matched across geographies.

quote.text: I would either copy this and just do a little bit better and run ads because I don't think these guys are ever going to run ads.

themes.watch: Sam owns Hampton, a paid founder community, and says he plans to eventually buy other communities, so he is talking up his own category. The $13-15M NADA figure is his guess, and the BNI price is a rumor.

themes.title: Moda Communities: vetted dealers fund 600,000 free members
themes.lead: Charge the sellers for trusted access to a pool of super-enthusiast buyers, and let the whales pay for everyone else.
bullets: Started in 2018 when the Sioux Falls founder wanted a better place to buy and sell watches; now 20-25 Facebook groups, 600,000 members, over a dozen full-time staff.
Groups split by tier: watches under $10k, over $10k, a superfan group above ~$100k, plus collectible cars and gold.
Dealers pass a vetting interview plus a second member's check, then pay $1-10k a year to post; Sam estimates $5-10M a year in revenue.
The founder's line to Sam: virtually everything is free and 'the top 1% or even the top 0.001% pay to keep everything running.'
Sam's moat argument, citing **Pieter Levels**: technology used to be a moat and isn't anymore; communities, networks and marketplaces still are.
themes.watch: Shaan's caveat: building on Facebook groups is dangerous because the platform keeps changing reach and member-add rules. The revenue range is Sam's estimate.

themes.title: Whales plus gacha: why card-pack 'ripping' apps hit $1B
themes.lead: Attach real resale value to a mystery-box mechanic, add an instant buyback, and a tiny slice of heavy spenders drives enormous revenue.
bullets: **Candy Crush**: 82M monthly actives, all revenue from 4% of players; the other 96% are 'the cost of finding those whales.'
Twitch gifted subs (~$5 each, 200 at once = ~$1,000) was 'like buying a bottle at the club' and lifted revenue per channel.
Shaan's co-founder was CTO of **AppLovin**, the biggest mobile-game ad network, and saw how games pay to acquire whales who spend across Candy Crush, Block Blast and FarmVille.
Mobile games set payout rates freely, unlike a regulated slot machine; a lapsed payer (30 days) gets a run of wins, then a frustrating wall built to make them pay again.
Ripping apps: pay $50 for a digital pack, get offered $43 back instantly; the company keeps $7 and reshuffles the card. One app did ~$1B last year, founded by an ex-Citadel/Bridgewater quant.
**Collector Crypt** runs ~$100M a month (visible on-chain); Logan Paul launched a rival, 'Rip It'; one of these apps went from ~$50k to $25M a month on the buyback 'vending machine' model.

Gacha (Japanese mystery capsules) got so popular Japan banned it, per Shaan, then spread to loot boxes in Overwatch and FIFA; real resale value (a top Pikachu card ~$15M) makes it stronger; a toy maker saw **7x** revenue putting the same products in mystery boxes.

quote.text: the genius of the thing was the buyback. The buyback changed everything.

themes.watch: Shaan himself calls it 'sad in a way' and likens it to a slot machine with no payout rules. The $1B and $25M-a-month figures came from a dinner conversation; he couldn't say how the revenue is counted (part GMV).

themes.title: Binance's $5B hack, and why Shaan still thinks DeFi is overlooked
themes.lead: The hack shows crypto's real tail risks, yet Shaan calls DeFi the next category to come back the way prediction markets did.
bullets: Shaan: the only crypto-only people left are 'high conviction diehards who deserve to get rich' and people who missed that everyone moved to AI.
Bitcoin's remaining big risks, in his view: Satoshi's coins moving, or AI/quantum breaking the encryption, either of which would cause 'extreme panic'.
**Binance** was hacked for $5B last week; its SAFU fund, built from 10% of trading fees since the 2018 hack, holds ~$2B, so it has to cover the gap.
Last report Shaan read: North Korea did it, via a woman in a romantic relationship with an engineer who got physical access to his laptop; part of the funds got frozen.
The hacker parked the coins in a DeFi lending protocol, borrowed stablecoins (up to ~50% of collateral) and walked away, so freezing the collateral didn't matter.
Shaan's analogy: early prediction markets like Augur died, then **Polymarket and Kalshi** broke out ~8 years later doing the same thing; he expects DeFi to follow.

quote.text: DeFi, by the way, is awesome and I think people are completely overlooking this and it's going to come back with the like the vengeance

themes.watch: The hack details are Shaan's account of early reporting ('last thing I read'). He is a former crypto investor who now calls himself an AI guy.

takeaways.title: Clone a dull, high-income profession's peer group and out-market it with ads
Charge the sellers or the top 1%, keep the crowd free
Build on networks and trust vetting, not on tech AI can copy
Study the buyback mechanic before you build or invest in collectibles apps
Treat exchange hacks and key-person laptops as live risks, not edge cases

hot_takes.take: I think communities, networks, and marketplaces are still a really good moat.
my goal is to build a multi-billion dollar company. And I think that we can get there by owning a variety of communities.
96% of the players are just kind of the cost of doing business which is the cost of finding those whales.
the only people left that are like true crypto only are the incredibly smart, high conviction dieards who deserve to get rich and the idiots
DeFi, by the way, is awesome and I think people are completely overlooking this and it's going to come back with the like the vengeance

other_news.title: **Private Photo Vault** (a hidden photo-storage app MFM discussed years ago) has ~1M ratings; the Vegas-raised founder told Sam it's 'a behemoth' (numbers off the record).
Sources referenced: Pieter Levels on AI and moats, Ev Williams' rule (find a universal desire, remove friction), a creator who reverse-engineers app algorithms like Tinder's.
Scale check: Snapchat does about $4B a year, which is why a $1B app nobody has heard of stood out.

glossary.def: A peer group of ~20 non-competing business owners who review each other's financials.
A tiny share of customers who spend far more than everyone else and fund the free users.
Japanese mystery-capsule mechanic; the template for loot boxes and blind boxes.
Opening card packs, now digital, with an instant buyback offer for unwanted pulls.
Binance's emergency user-protection fund, fed by 10% of trading fees.
Permissionless protocols that lend against posted crypto collateral and auto-liquidate if it falls.
